$comment: Deterministic rule catalogue for un-editorial-check. The editorial set (profile: null) is the default; every other set runs only through an explicit audit profile. Validated by lib/config.mjs and asserted against lib/rules.mjs and lib/audits.mjs by the test suite.

rules.guardNotes: Allowlisted terms, quoted titles, URLs, code and comments are outside the extracted copy span and cannot fire. The -ize/-ise conflict family is a profile choice: a default run warns, un-secretariat-document and un-geneva-web accept it, generic-british-english enforces -ise.
rules.summary: American spelling used in prose where the profile prescribes the British form.

rules.guardNotes: Emitted per copy block, independently of UE-SP001, so mixed register is visible even when one variant is allowlisted.
rules.summary: British and American variants of the same word used in one passage.

rules.guardNotes: Silent unless spellingReview is true; matching is case-insensitive; size and prize forms are not -ise candidates and are skipped; some -ize spellings are standard (Oxford) and are never claimed as errors.
rules.summary: -ize form that may require an -ise spelling under the named dictionary.

rules.guardNotes: Profile pairs are matched as written; a term inside a definition context is downgraded to warning with heuristic confidence, where naming the unapproved term may be intentional. The one gated pair, "maternal mortality rate", is review-only: a warning with heuristic confidence is raised only when a printed statistic sits within 120 characters before and 200 characters after the term, the message quotes the printed per-100 000 live-births figure when one is present and says plainly that the denominator could not be determined offline when it is not, and a term with no printed statistic in the window raises no finding. No gated finding ever carries a replacement, so --fix cannot reach it.
rules.summary: Unapproved indicator or programme term from the organisation profile, with a context-gated review flag for the causal maternal mortality formulation.

rules.guardNotes: Phrase-aware match on the exact configured term; allowlist entries are checked first. Only pairs with a recorded source are configured: the unsourced "women's work" and "female work" replacement pairs were removed from the profile, so no wording is proposed that a recorded source does not support. Report-only — no replacement is passed, so --fix never rewrites it.
rules.summary: Unapproved gender, age or population phrasing from the organisation profile.

rules.guardNotes: Silent in every context: the live manual permits the percentage sign in running text, and resolution context has no deterministic offline detector because the checker does not resolve agenda symbols or document types — that branch is a documented limitation in rules/terminology.md, not a heuristic guess. The rule keeps its id, suppressions and configuration switch so a future detector can be switched on without a format change. The per cent spelling preference belongs to UE-SP001.
rules.summary: Percentage sign in running prose: silent by design, because the manual permits both forms and resolution context cannot be detected offline.

rules.guardNotes: The suggestion accounts for a preceding the; U.S.A., US dollar and cent amounts and US$ currency figures are excluded. Report-only: no replacement is passed, so --fix never rewrites the finding and an editor writes the full name by hand.
rules.summary: Bare US used as a country name in prose.

rules.guardNotes: Superseded country designations are matched case-sensitively: the lowercase turkey is the bird and never fires, and only the exact written form or the all-caps heading form is the country name. A match inside a multi-word proper name (North Macedonia, North Holland, Wild Turkey) is exempt through the proper-name guard, so the correct current form never reports itself. Detection is data-driven from the profile’s UE-TE005 pairs, each mapped to the current United Nations designation recorded in the source registry. Report-only: no replacement is passed, so --fix never rewrites it, and historical or non-editorial contexts can be allowlisted per project with config.allowlist.terminology.
rules.summary: Superseded country name written where the current United Nations designation is required.

rules.guardNotes: Slash-delimited dates and the written month-first form (March 5, 2026) are both reported. ISO machine dates inside URLs and code are outside the copy span; full month names only, so an abbreviated month is out of scope; a month-year reference (March 2026) and the correct day-month-year order never match. Dates are never rewritten by --fix: the finding carries proposed wording, not a replacement.
rules.summary: Numeric or month-first date instead of the day-month-year written form.

rules.guardNotes: Skipped in compact surfaces; already-en-dashed ranges and version numbers never match.
rules.summary: Numeric range joined with a hyphen instead of an en dash.

rules.guardNotes: Phrase-aware; approved and allowlisted phrases are exempt, and quoted titles are outside the span.
rules.summary: Promotional or non-neutral register term in prose.

rules.guardNotes: The CLI cannot prove or disprove a ranking claim; it routes the claim to review rather than asserting a defect. The fixed economic term "leading indicator" is exempt because it names an indicator, not a ranking.
rules.summary: Superlative or ranking claim that needs a source or neutral wording.

rules.guardNotes: Clause-level: one hedged sentence does not hedge the next. Figures without a unit word are not prose figures.
rules.summary: Figure stated without a hedge or source in the same sentence.

rules.guardNotes: Sentence-initial question openers ending in a question mark only; a genuine information question can match the same openers, so the sentence is routed to review as a heuristic and never declared a defect.
rules.summary: Rhetorical question used for effect where UN copy states the finding directly.

rules.guardNotes: Comparison operators and shouting markers preceded by =, !, < or > are excluded.
rules.summary: Exclamation mark in formal copy.

rules.guardNotes: A qualifier in the count's own sentence (reported, estimated, total, as of, more than) satisfies the rule; a qualifier in the next sentence does not. The counted-noun list is bounded and covers the nouns humanitarian and programme copy counts — countries, refugees, children, cases, deaths, households and their peers; a count of an unlisted noun is not reported.
rules.summary: Count that does not say what was counted or whether it is reported, estimated or total.

rules.guardNotes: Requires both multiple years and an explicit comparison phrase; a single year in prose never fires.
rules.summary: Comparison that may be aligning different reference periods.

rules.guardNotes: Exists only when --claims verifies a register. An entry with no recorded source, or with a source but no reference date, is one finding each; the check verifies that the bookkeeping happened, never that the claim is true. Severity warning by default, escalatable through config.severities; the finding carries no replacement, so --fix cannot reach it. A stale entry (the claim text no longer appears in the copy) is reported on the status line and never fails the run.
rules.summary: A claim register entry is missing its source or reference date.

rules.guardNotes: Exists only when --claims verifies a register. Every claim-shaped detection (UE-RE002, UE-RE003, UE-DI001, UE-CL001) in the scan must have a register entry whose file and claim text match; a detection with none is one finding. The match is on normalised claim text, so an edit that reflowed whitespace does not orphan an entry, while a changed figure does. The finding asks that the claim be tracked, and never judges whether the claim is true; it is never fixable.
rules.summary: A claim detected in the scan is not recorded in the claim register.

rules.guardNotes: Bare status assertions only: claims attributed to a reporting party, quoted copy, comments and URLs never reach the rule. Detection is symmetric — every claimant in an entry fires on the same pattern — and each knowledge-base entry cites its source. Since Wave 3 the knowledge base also covers negation, corpus-variant and incomplete-assertion forms through lib/diplomacy-ext.mjs (compiled by lib/rules-hs.mjs into this same rule id); the attribution guard and config.allowlist.claims suppression apply to those forms unchanged, and the extension never matches a bare status word or an unlisted region. Severity is warning: the finding requires diplomatic review and is never a claim that the text is factually false, so a status-sensitivity judgement alone does not fail a build — escalate deliberately with config.severities. The finding is routed to the diplomacy lane.
rules.summary: Contested sovereignty or territorial-status claim about a listed region stated as fact instead of attributed or phrased in neutral United Nations terminology.

rules.guardNotes: Length measured after entity decoding and whitespace normalisation; never affects the exit code.
rules.summary: Page title missing, empty or longer than the recommended maximum.

rules.guardNotes: Length measured after entity decoding; never affects the exit code.
rules.summary: Meta description missing, empty or longer than the recommended maximum.

rules.guardNotes: Validates declaration syntax and, when configured, the origin; it does not fetch the URL or prove path self-reference.
rules.summary: Canonical link missing, relative, or pointing at a different origin.

rules.guardNotes: Counts literal h1 openings outside comments and scripts is not attempted; it is an audit, not editorial copy.
rules.summary: Page does not have exactly one first-level heading.

rules.guardNotes: Informational only; social cards are a publishing concern, not an editorial one.
rules.summary: Open Graph or Twitter card metadata missing.

rules.guardNotes: Attribute-presence check only; it cannot judge whether the accessible name is a good one.
rules.summary: Image, canvas or embedded content without an accessible name or alt attribute.

rules.guardNotes: Associates by aria-label, aria-labelledby or a matching label for; it does not verify visual placement.
rules.summary: Form control without an associated label.

rules.guardNotes: Flags every innerHTML/outerHTML assignment without tracing taint; it reports a sink, never an exploit.
rules.summary: Assignment to a DOM HTML sink that can execute injected markup.

rules.guardNotes: Reads integrity and crossorigin attributes only; never fetches the asset and never validates the hash.
rules.summary: Remote script or stylesheet without a Subresource Integrity attribute.

rules.guardNotes: Attribute-presence check on the anchor itself; rel=noopener or rel=noreferrer satisfies it.
rules.summary: target="_blank" link opened without rel=noopener or rel=noreferrer.

rules.guardNotes: Flags eval and the Function constructor outright; it reports a capability, never a proven execution path.
rules.summary: Dynamic code execution through eval or the Function constructor.

rules.guardNotes: Composition over word lists: a finding requires a listed dehumanising frame predicated of a listed group of people, so the frame word alone never matches. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS002 and UE-HS003, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy, block quotations, comments and URLs never reach the rule because extraction masks those spans before any rule runs. The rule reports the matched wording as an error with deterministic confidence and passes no replacement for --fix; proposed wording is review guidance only and the finding is never fixable. A finding flags wording for human review and never asserts that any sentence meets the legal threshold of incitement.
rules.summary: A listed group of people predicated of a listed dehumanising, pest, disease or animal frame in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Universal-quantifier and inherent-trait forms only: an accusation noun without a quantifier does not match, while a trait predicate of the group matches with or without an inherent marker. A negated universal such as "Not all foreigners are criminals" is excluded as a hedged or corrected statement. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS001 and UE-HS003, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy never reaches the rule. This rule is a heuristic: every finding says it is routed to review and never claims proof of intent, because the pattern shows collective framing rather than the state of mind of the speaker. Severity is warning — a heuristic judgement question must never fail a build on its own — and the finding is routed to the harmful-discriminatory review lane for high-severity human review. No replacement is passed, proposed wording is review guidance only, and the finding is never fixable.
rules.summary: Collective blame or an inherent trait attributed to a whole listed group of people in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Base-form verbs and modal outcome constructions only: a past-tense narrative such as "Attackers killed the refugees in the camp" is not a call and never matches. The rule matches group-level demands, never individual legal process, so due-process wording about named or counted individuals stays silent. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS001 and UE-HS002, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy never reaches the rule. The rule is deterministic, severity is error, and it is report-only: no finding carries a replacement, while proposed wording is review guidance only.
rules.summary: A call for exclusion or violence against a listed group of people rather than individual legal process in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Composition over word lists: each of the three branches must pair vocabulary with demeaning context — a listed protected group predicated of a demeaning predicate, a disability term within one 300-character window of pity framing, or a disability term beside a first-person person-rejection — and no branch ever matches on its vocabulary alone. Anaphoric subjects such as "They are a burden" are not resolved: the rule stays silent rather than guessing at the referent. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy never reaches the rule. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS001, UE-HS002 and UE-HS003, so expanding a protected characteristic keeps every mirrored sentence in those rules firing identically. Severity is error — high-severity human review — but the finding is report-only: no finding carries a replacement, nothing is ever rewritten automatically, and the matched wording is never a legal judgement. The finding is routed to the harmful-discriminatory review lane.
rules.summary: Demeaning predicate, pity framing or first-person person-rejection about a listed protected group or disability term in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Appellation shapes only — an article-led singular ("a clown") or a bare plural ("idiots") — matched on extracted copy, so quoted copy and block quotations are outside the span while a paraphrase in the writer's own voice still matches. The rule cannot judge the target or context: criticism of a policy may use the same wording, so every finding is routed to review as a warning, never declared a defect.
rules.summary: Direct insult, name-calling or contempt appellation aimed at a person or group.

rules.guardNotes: Fixed-phrase matching cannot separate a threat from idiom: the sports sentence "the squad will regret the missed penalty" matches and is routed to review, while the finance and sports collocations "crush expectations" and "crush records" are deliberately excluded by pattern — both sides are locked by fixtures. The rule never proves a threat; confidence is heuristic.
rules.summary: Threat or intimidation posture written as a fixed phrase in prose.

rules.guardNotes: The pattern proves only that an all-caps token of five or more letters stands alone: no adjacent word character, digit, hyphen or slash, and no file-name extension after it, so short initialisms fall outside it by length alone. The exemption list is finite (UNHCR, ECOSOC, SARIF, README, USAGE …) and an initialism, heading or reference word missing from it is reported, because the rule cannot tell a heading from shouting.
rules.summary: All-caps word of five letters or more in running prose.

rules.guardNotes: Case-insensitive match on two identical words in a row; the legitimate doubles had had, that that and very very are exempt (fixture gr-doubles-ok.txt). One space or a run of spaces between the words matches: a padded pair reaches the rule through the collapsed copy span and is proved against the unit's own source slice through the offset map, so the fix covers the real bytes and hard-wrapped joins never match. Punctuation between the words never matches, so intentional repetition outside the exemption list (for example long long ago) is still reported and may need ue:ignore.
rules.summary: Unintentionally doubled word, for example the the.

rules.guardNotes: Covers exactly one space between a word and one of , . ; : ? !; only the space is reported — the presence of an exclamation mark belongs to UE-RE005. Multiple spaces before the mark, a mark that starts a hard-wrapped line and an ellipsis after the space are not matched; URLs, quotations and code are outside the copy span.
rules.summary: A space between a word and its following punctuation.

rules.guardNotes: Excludes a period preceded by another period or the ellipsis character, a period preceded by a digit (decimals such as 1.5, version numbers such as v1.2, outline numbering), single-letter initials and dotted initial chains (U.S.A., U.K., e.g., i.e., J.P.), and the abbreviations U.S., U.K., U.N., e.g., i.e., etc., Dr., Mr., Mrs., Prof., vs., a.m., p.m. and St. written directly against the next word; a period followed by a lower-case letter (index.js) never matches. The list is a conservative exemption: any other period abutting a capital — an abbreviation outside the list included — is reported, since a space is required after it, and a single-letter word ending a sentence before a capital (Annex A.The) is skipped with the initials.
rules.summary: A full stop running straight into the next word instead of ending the sentence.

rules.guardNotes: Silent unless config.spacingReview is true. Detection reads the unit's own source slice through the offset map, because the copy span collapses whitespace runs: two or more literal spaces between words inside authored copy are reported, and the replacement is a single space. A run whose first character is a tab or a newline (indentation or a hard-wrapped line join) never matches, and a run the line break closes is a Markdown hard-line-break marker and never matches. Navigation, compact and every non-authored context are out of scope; deliberately aligned plain-text columns will report when the review is switched on, so silence a span with ue:ignore or leave the review off.
rules.summary: A run of two or more spaces between words in prose (configuration-gated review).

rules.guardNotes: Heuristic only, not a complete grammar check: authored prose is split into sentences and only the first suspect sentence per block is reported, with verb presence judged from auxiliaries and modals, the word endings -s, -ed and -ing, and a curated base-verb list, so a base verb missing from that list remains a false positive risk. Sentences containing a comma, parentheses, an abbreviation tail, a repeated content word of five letters or more, fewer than five or more than eight words, and every heading, list item, compact or non-authored unit are skipped; detection is per block, so quoted, code, navigation and cross-block copy are out of scope.
rules.summary: A five- to eight-word sentence-like string ending in a full stop but carrying no finite verb — a phrase standing where a sentence should be.

rules.guardNotes: Heuristic pattern matching, not a complete grammar check: only three tight collocations are recognised — modal verbs followed by of (excluding the idiomatic of course), had, have, has or did followed by went, and more or less followed by better or worse — so every other malformed wording is missed by design. Code and other non-authored units are never matched, the rule is report-only and emits a suggestion with no replacement, and each occurrence is reported as its own finding.
rules.summary: Malformed wording such as could of, had went or more better, reported with the standard-English form as a suggestion.

rules.guardNotes: Heuristic duplication check, not a complete repetition audit: it runs in two forms. A sentence of four or more words is normalised (lower-cased, punctuation stripped) and compared against other sentences in the same extracted block; and an authored block of twenty words or more is normalised the same way and compared against earlier blocks in the same file, so a paragraph inserted twice is reported at the second occurrence with the first line named in the message. A block is a whole paragraph, not a piece of extracted text: the pieces of a paragraph an inline element split are rejoined on what a reader sees between them, so bold, italics, a link or a highlighted span inside one copy of a duplicated paragraph splits neither copy below the floor and cannot hide the repeat, whether the element wraps whole words or breaks one word in half. The one limit is an image or a break inside the paragraph: the copy either side of it is joined with a space, because that is what a reader sees there too. The twenty-word floor is a deliberate boundary rather than a tuned one: it sits above the length at which two paragraphs sharing a sentence is ordinary cross-referencing, and measured over this repository and the bundled corpora it yields only the inserted paragraph in the adversarial web corpus. Both forms stay silent on quoted, cited, code and metadata copy, on headings, on compact table units, and on copy whose extraction context is navigation: HTML nav, menu, aside and their label attributes. Navigation is the one silence a Markdown document cannot have, because it has no navigation surface and every paragraph in it is authored copy; so a paragraph repeated inside one Markdown file is reported, and a standing disclaimer or a repeated mandate is reported with it. The comparison is per file, so the same paragraph in two different files is never reported whatever its purpose; within one file it always is. Near-duplicates, paraphrases, repeated headings, repeated short fragments and repetition across files are out of scope. Sentences shorter than four words and blocks shorter than twenty words are too short to judge, at most one finding per block keeps the report readable, and no replacement is passed, so a duplicated block is never rewritten.
rules.summary: The same sentence repeated inside one block, or a long authored block repeated verbatim later in the same file.

rules.guardNotes: Heuristic heading-style check, not a complete punctuation audit: only heading units in authored or navigation copy are tested, and only for a terminal full stop or semicolon. Other trailing punctuation, headings without terminal punctuation, setext (underlined) headings that the extractor does not flag as headings, and paragraph text that merely ends in a full stop are all out of scope; the rule is report-only with a suggestion and no replacement.
rules.summary: A heading ending in a full stop or semicolon, so it reads as a sentence instead of a label.

rules.guardNotes: Heuristic quotation check, not a complete typography audit: balanced straight and curly quote pairs are masked before the rules run, so only a mark that survives that masking is reported, while apostrophes are ignored entirely. Marks inside code or compact navigation units are skipped, a quotation split across lines or blocks cannot be paired and is therefore out of scope, and each surviving mark is reported with a suggestion rather than a replacement.
rules.summary: An unpaired quotation mark left in the copy — opened but never closed in the same unit.

rules.guardNotes: Whole-document review: an uppercase letter run of three to five letters whose expansion is never given anywhere in the same file is reported once, at its first authored occurrence. The window is deliberate: digits, hyphens and dotted forms are out of scope (COVID-19, G7, U.S.A. never match), a file name (CHANGELOG.md), a version or figure position (PHP 8+) and the established initialisms the all-caps register rule accepts are exempt, and the three-to-five ceiling keeps shouted English words (DEFEAT, DEMANDS), which the register rule already reports, out of the acronym rule; longer established initialisms (UNFCCC, UNAIDS) are missed by the same window and are the documented cost. Expansion detection requires a word sequence whose initials spell the acronym, contiguous, within 200 characters of a parenthetical use; expansions whose initials are interrupted by small words (Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs for OCHA) are not recognised, which is the cost of never inventing a definition. Judged over authored copy, per file; a house acronym is allowlisted with config.allowlist.acronyms. The finding asks for the first-use expansion United Nations editorial guidance requires and is never fixable. The check is a heuristic: a longer acronym outside the window, an expansion the matcher cannot recognise and an initialism the lists miss are all false-negative or false-positive costs the window and the exemption set accept.
rules.summary: Short acronym used without an expansion anywhere in the document.

rules.guardNotes: Per-paragraph honesty note: when an authored paragraph of forty or more words carries fewer than six per cent common English stop words, the passage probably is not English, and every rule in this tool is written for English copy. Judged per paragraph rather than per file because United Nations documents are routinely bilingual in passing, so a whole-file ratio would stay silent exactly when one long non-English passage needs the note. The finding is informational, is emitted once per qualifying paragraph, claims no language identification (a stop-word rate is not a detector) and never suppresses the other rules; its purpose is to stop a clean run or a page of findings being read as a check the tool cannot perform. The check is a heuristic, not a language detector: a stop-word rate cannot identify a language, so the note claims only that the rules may not apply.
rules.summary: A long paragraph does not appear to be English, and the rules are English-only.

rules.guardNotes: Silent unless config.consistencyReview is true. Whole-document consistency: paired straight and paired typographic quotation marks both appearing in the authored copy of one file are a finding, because one quotation style should carry a document. Unpaired marks belong to UE-HR005; quoted-material spans are outside the scan; JavaScript string delimiters and HTML attribute quotes never reach a copy unit. Info severity: the check says the document is internally inconsistent, never which style is right, and is never fixable. The check is a heuristic about document conventions, not a complete typography audit.
rules.summary: Both straight and typographic quotation marks are used in one document (configuration-gated review).

rules.guardNotes: Silent unless config.consistencyReview is true. Whole-document consistency: comma-grouped (1,000) and space-grouped (1 000) thousands separators both appearing in the authored copy of one file are a finding, because one grouping convention should carry a document. Compact table units are outside the scan; a number followed by a hyphen, slash or digit never matches the space-grouped form. Info severity: the check names the inconsistency, never which convention is right, and is never fixable. The check is a heuristic about document conventions, not a complete typography audit.
rules.summary: Both comma-grouped and space-grouped numbers are used in one document (configuration-gated review).

rules.source: user-supplied glossary (--glossary / config.glossary), not a United Nations rule
rules.limitation: The term list comes from the reader's own JSON file, which has no URL, no retrieval date and no institutional authority: the checker can prove the wording is on that list, never that the reader's term is correct. Which file it is, and which declared term matched, are on the finding as structured fields and in its message.
rules.action: Decide the house wording yourself and write it into the source. The checker never rewrites a glossary term, whatever the glossary declares as a replacement.
rules.guardNotes: Reader-supplied check, not a United Nations rule: the term list comes from the reader's own JSON file, which has no URL, no retrieval date and no institutional authority, so it is never recorded in rules/sources.json and is always labelled user-supplied in the finding message. Matching is literal, case-insensitive and whole-word over the extracted copy span, so quoted, cited, code, URL and comment regions cannot fire. The source field names the mechanism, not a file, because a rule entry cannot know which path the reader passed; the finding's message and its structured glossary.file carry the actual path. Neither rule passes a replacement and neither id is on the --fix allow-list, so terminology is never rewritten automatically. Warning severity is the default a reader sees, but it is not what protects the exit code: the finding is audit-lane, and lib/output.mjs editorialErrors filters audit-lane findings out of the exit code whatever severity they carry. A reader who re-grades this rule to error through config.severities still gets exit 0, and the finding is still reported in the audit section. The invariant is locked at error severity in tests/audit-lanes.mjs section 6b.
rules.summary: A term the reader's own glossary forbids appears in user-visible copy.

rules.source: user-supplied glossary (--glossary / config.glossary), not a United Nations rule
rules.limitation: The required-term list comes from the reader's own JSON file, which has no URL, no retrieval date and no institutional authority: the checker can prove the term is absent from a file, never that the concept belongs in it. The unit of judgement is the file, because that is what the reader's promise is about.
rules.action: Write the required wording into the passage the concept belongs to. The checker cannot decide which passage that is, and never rewrites a glossary term.
rules.guardNotes: Reader-supplied check, not a United Nations rule: the required-term list comes from the reader's own JSON file, which has no URL, no retrieval date and no institutional authority, so it is never recorded in rules/sources.json and is always labelled user-supplied in the finding message. The unit of judgement is the file, because the promise is that this document must call the concept by this term: a file whose extracted copy never contains the term raises one finding anchored at line 1, column 1, and a file that produced no copy spans at all raises none, since nothing was read to judge. Whitespace between the words of a phrase is flexible, which can under-report an absence but never invent a position, and a file carrying ue:ignore all is silent. No replacement is passed and the id is not on the --fix allow-list, so terminology is never rewritten automatically. Warning severity is the default a reader sees, but it is not what protects the exit code: the finding is audit-lane, and lib/output.mjs editorialErrors filters audit-lane findings out of the exit code whatever severity they carry. A reader who re-grades this rule to error through config.severities still gets exit 0, and the finding is still reported in the audit section. The invariant is locked at error severity in tests/audit-lanes.mjs section 6b.
rules.summary: A term the reader's own glossary requires does not appear anywhere in a scanned file.
